questions.problem: The rate, in degrees Farhenheit per month, at which the average midday temperature in New York City varies, does so according to the function $R(t)={t}^{3}+3,$ where $t$ is the number of months since the measurements began. Estimate the total increase in air temperature over the first three months using the trapezoidal rule with $3$ trapezoids of equal height.
questions.worked_solution:
In this context, the area $A$ under the curve $y=R(t)$ over the interval $[0,3]$ represents the total increase in air temperature over the first three months.

The general formula for the trapezoidal rule states that

$$
A≈\frac{1}{2}[R(a)+2(R({t}_{1})+R({t}_{2})+⋯+R({t}_{n-1}))+R(b)]Δt,
$$

where $n$ is the number of trapezoids and $Δt=\frac{b-a}{n}$ is the step size.

Here, we have the following values:

- The number of trapezoids is $n=3.$

- The corresponding interval is $[0,3],$ so we have $a=0$ and $b=3.$

- The step size is given by

$$
Δt=\frac{b-a}{n}=\frac{3-0}{3}=1.
$$

Using the above values, the general formula becomes

$$
A≈\frac{1}{2}[R(0)+2(R(1)+R(2))+R(3)]\cdot 1.
$$

To identify the function values, we now set up a table with the values of $t$ and $R(t):$

| $t$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R(t)$ | $3$ | $4$ | $11$ | $30$ |

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the above expression gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈\frac{1}{2}[3+2(4+11)+30]\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{63}{2} \\  & =31.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total air temperature increase is approximately ${31.5}^{∘}\,\text{F}.$

questions.problem:
Using the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[-1,2]=[-1,0]\cup [0,2],
$$

approximate the area under the curve of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ whose data is given in the table below.

| $x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot what this function might look like, using the values given in the table.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14274355/assets/5bce94e0d39fc714bed04f254e98d092010256c9eb440dc6bc26f61f2f0e38cb.png)

We've drawn some trapezoids to help calculate our trapezoidal rule sum. By calculating the area of each trapezoid, we obtain the following approximation for our area $A:$

$$
A≈\overset{1\text{st trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(-1)+f(0)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{1}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}+\overset{2\text{nd trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(0)+f(2)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{2}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}
$$

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the above expression gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈\frac{1+3}{2}\cdot (0-(-1))+\frac{3+2}{2}\cdot (2-0) \\  & =2\cdot 1+\frac{5}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =2+5 \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[0,5]=[0,2]\cup [2,5],
$$

approximate the area under the curve of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ whose data is given in the table below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $3$ | $1$ | $4$ |
questions.worked_solution:

We've drawn some trapezoids to help calculate our trapezoidal rule sum. By calculating the area of each trapezoid, we obtain the following approximation for our area $A:$

$$
A≈\overset{1\text{st trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(0)+f(2)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{1}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}+\overset{2\text{nd trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(2)+f(5)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{2}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}
$$

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the above expression gives

$$

$$

questions.problem:
An empty tank starts filling with water according to the function $v(t)={t}^{2}-3t+7,$ in liters per minute. Use the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[0,2]\cup [2,5]\cup [5,7],
$$

to approximate the total amount of water in the tank the first $7$ minutes.
questions.worked_solution:
In this context, we have $3$ trapezoids, and the area $A$ under the curve $y=v(t)$ represents the total amount of water in the tank the first $7$ minutes.

Using the trapezoidal rule, we estimate the area as follows:

$$
A≈\frac{v(0)+v(2)}{2}\cdot Δ{t}_{1}+\frac{v(2)+v(5)}{2}\cdot Δ{t}_{2}+\frac{v(5)+v(7)}{2}\cdot Δ{t}_{3}
$$

To identify the function values, we now set up a table with the values of $t$ and $v(t):$

| $t$ | $0$ | $2$ | $5$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)$ | $7$ | $5$ | $17$ | $35$ |

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the approximation for $A$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈\frac{7+5}{2}\cdot (2-0)+\frac{5+17}{2}\cdot (5-2)+\frac{17+35}{2}\cdot (7-5) \\  & =6(2)+11(3)+26(2) \\  & =12+33+52 \\  & =97.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total amount of water in the tank is approximately $97\,\text{liters}$ the first $7$ minutes.
